ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Madam C. J. Walker

code.originalText: Eleven-week review: home readings on maximum losartan, urine albumin, kidney function after a recent gastroenteritis, lipids on atorvastatin

text.paragraph: Eleven-week review: home readings on maximum losartan, urine albumin, kidney function after a recent gastroenteritis, lipids on atorvastatin. [S]

Madam Walker returns two weeks after her sick visit for gastroenteritis. The vomiting and diarrhea settled within two days, and she restarted losartan and empagliflozin once she had eaten normally for a day. The potassium and creatinine check due two to four weeks after the losartan increase was not done: she was on a three-week convention tour and her office had booked no laboratory day. The panel planned for the week after the sick visit was also missed when she left on another trip. Her home readings on losartan 100 mg average 134/84. She has had no dizziness, cough, genital itching or muscle aches. She is asking for sauces on the side and no added salt at banquets. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 136/86, pulse 76; weight 77.2 kg

Albumin in the urine (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 286 mg/g) with eGFR 54 by the race-free CKD-EPI 2021 equation; she recalls protein in the urine at an executive physical a year ago, and those records are requested; to be repeated and investigated
S — Synthetic presenting finding, superseded by the kidney diagnosis at two weeks.

Hypertension, stage 2, confirmed by 24-hour ambulatory monitoring (24-hour mean 149/94, daytime 154/98, night 140/88 without the normal nighttime fall), with left ventricular hypertrophy on ECG and mild hypertensive retinopathy; synthetic modern episode linked to her documented high blood pressure
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to the documented hypertension and nephritis.

Chronic kidney disease G3a A2 (eGFR 54 to 55 mL/min/1.73 m2 by the race-free CKD-EPI 2021 equation; albumin-to-creatinine ratio 286 to 294 mg/g; present for more than three months), most likely hypertensive kidney disease; bland urine sediment and normal-sized kidneys on ultrasound; 5-year kidney failure risk 1.6%
S — Synthetic kidney findings anchored to the documented nephritis and death from kidney disease.
Hyperlipidemia: LDL 174 mg/dL; 10-year ASCVD risk 7.9% by the Pooled Cohort Equations (intermediate)
Viral gastroenteritis after a sales convention, with mild volume depletion and losartan and empagliflozin held under her sick-day rules; no acute kidney injury; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness; not a historical claim.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease (2024); KDIGO 2021 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Blood Pressure in Chronic Kidney Disease (2021); 2018 AHA/ACC/AACVPR/AAPA/ABC/ACPM/ADA/AGS/APhA/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol (2018); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, hyperlipidemia and depression monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Preventive visit in about six weeks. Six-month review in the summer with urine albumin, kidney function and hemoglobin, booked on a home day. Call for ankle swelling, dizziness, or vomiting or diarrhea (hold losartan and empagliflozin). Next scheduled visit 2026-06-08: periodic adult preventive visit. [S]
